test_cases.test_name: Verify Standard Item Master Creation and Tracking
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system can successfully create and track standard inventory items including raw materials, packaging components, and finished goods.
prerequisites: Access to the inventory management system with appropriate user roles.
List of sample raw materials, packaging components, and finished goods with their details (e.g., SKU, description, unit of measure).

test_steps.action: Navigate to the Item Master creation module within the inventory management system.
test_steps.expected_result: The Item Master creation screen is displayed, allowing for the input of item details.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the Item Master creation screen.

test_steps.action: Create a new item record for a raw material (e.g., 'API-XYZ', 'Unit: KG').
test_steps.expected_result: The raw material item is successfully created and saved in the system.
data_to_capture: Item ID of the created raw material.

test_steps.action: Create a new item record for a packaging component (e.g., 'BOTTLE-100ML', 'Unit: EA').
test_steps.expected_result: The packaging component item is successfully created and saved in the system.
data_to_capture: Item ID of the created packaging component.

test_steps.action: Create a new item record for a finished good (e.g., 'PRODUCT-ABC', 'Unit: BOX').
test_steps.expected_result: The finished good item is successfully created and saved in the system.
data_to_capture: Item ID of the created finished good.

test_steps.action: Search for the created raw material, packaging component, and finished good items in the system.
test_steps.expected_result: All three created items are found and their details are displayed accurately.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of search results showing all three items.

acceptance_criteria: All three types of inventory items (raw material, packaging component, finished good) are successfully created and retrievable.
Item details are accurately reflected in the system after creation.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-002: Track raw materials, packaging components, and finished goods using standard item master.
data_integrity_requirements: Item master data must be accurate and complete.
No data corruption during item creation.

test_cases.test_name: Verify FIFO and FEFO Inventory Rotation Logic
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system correctly implements First-In-First-Out (FIFO) and First-Expired-First-Out (FEFO) inventory rotation logic for stock management.
prerequisites: Access to the inventory management system with appropriate user roles.
At least two batches of the same raw material with different receipt dates and expiry dates.
System configured to support FIFO and FEFO.

test_steps.action: Receive Batch A of a raw material with an earlier receipt date and an earlier expiry date (e.g., Receipt Date: 2023-01-01, Expiry Date: 2024-01-01).
test_steps.expected_result: Batch A is successfully recorded in inventory with its associated receipt and expiry dates.
data_to_capture: Inventory record for Batch A showing receipt and expiry dates.

test_steps.action: Receive Batch B of the same raw material with a later receipt date and a later expiry date (e.g., Receipt Date: 2023-02-01, Expiry Date: 2024-02-01).
test_steps.expected_result: Batch B is successfully recorded in inventory with its associated receipt and expiry dates.
data_to_capture: Inventory record for Batch B showing receipt and expiry dates.

test_steps.action: Initiate a stock pick for a quantity of the raw material, ensuring the system defaults to FIFO.
test_steps.expected_result: The system proposes to pick from Batch A first, as it was received earlier.
data_to_capture: Picking list or system prompt showing Batch A as the primary pick source.

test_steps.action: Receive Batch C of the same raw material with an earlier expiry date than Batch B but a later receipt date (e.g., Receipt Date: 2023-03-01, Expiry Date: 2023-12-31).
test_steps.expected_result: Batch C is successfully recorded in inventory with its associated receipt and expiry dates.
data_to_capture: Inventory record for Batch C showing receipt and expiry dates.

test_steps.action: Initiate a stock pick for a quantity of the raw material, ensuring the system defaults to FEFO.
test_steps.expected_result: The system proposes to pick from Batch C first, as it has the earliest expiry date.
data_to_capture: Picking list or system prompt showing Batch C as the primary pick source.

acceptance_criteria: The system correctly prioritizes Batch A for picking when FIFO is applied.
The system correctly prioritizes Batch C for picking when FEFO is applied, overriding the receipt date.
Inventory rotation logic is applied as expected based on receipt and expiry dates.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-003: Implement First-In-First-Out (FIFO) inventory rotation using vendor default algorithms.
URS-INV-004: Support First-Expired-First-Out (FEFO) rotation for expiry date management.
data_integrity_requirements: Accurate tracking of receipt dates and expiry dates for all inventory batches.
Correct application of FIFO and FEFO logic to prevent stock obsolescence or expiry.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Real-time Inventory Quantity Tracking and Barcode Scanning
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system accurately tracks inventory quantities in real-time and supports barcode scanning for inventory movements.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
Item master data is populated.
Barcode scanner is connected and functional.

test_steps.action: Perform a manual inventory adjustment for a specific SKU, increasing its quantity.
test_steps.expected_result: The system reflects the updated inventory quantity for the SKU in real-time.

test_steps.action: Scan the barcode of the same SKU during a simulated receiving or put-away process.
test_steps.expected_result: The system correctly identifies the SKU via barcode scan and updates its quantity accordingly.

test_steps.action: Perform a manual inventory adjustment for a specific SKU, decreasing its quantity.
test_steps.expected_result: The system reflects the updated inventory quantity for the SKU in real-time.

test_steps.action: Scan the barcode of the same SKU during a simulated picking process.
test_steps.expected_result: The system correctly identifies the SKU via barcode scan and decrements its quantity accordingly.

acceptance_criteria: Inventory quantities are updated and displayed accurately within 30 seconds of any adjustment or scan.
Barcode scanning correctly identifies SKUs and initiates the appropriate inventory transaction (increase or decrease).
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-006: Track inventory quantities in real-time using standard database updates.
URS-INV-007: Support barcode scanning using vendor's barcode integration module.
data_integrity_requirements: All inventory quantity changes must be accurately recorded.
Barcode scan data must be correctly interpreted and mapped to the corresponding SKU.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Cycle Count Scheduling and Inventory Movement Reporting
test_cases.objective: To verify the system's ability to generate cycle count schedules and produce standard inventory movement reports.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
Sufficient inventory data exists for reporting.
User has permissions to generate reports and schedule counts.

test_steps.action: Configure and generate a cycle count schedule for a specific location or set of SKUs using the vendor's standard scheduling engine.
test_steps.expected_result: A cycle count schedule is generated, listing the items and locations to be counted.
data_to_capture: Cycle count schedule parameters (e.g., frequency, scope)

test_steps.action: Perform a physical count for a subset of items on the generated cycle count schedule and record the results in the system.
test_steps.expected_result: The system accepts the physical count data and flags any discrepancies.

test_steps.action: Generate an inventory movement report for a defined period using a pre-built template.
test_steps.expected_result: The system generates an inventory movement report that accurately reflects all recorded inventory transactions within the specified period.

test_steps.action: Verify that the inventory movement report includes details such as item, quantity, movement type, date, and user.
test_steps.expected_result: All relevant inventory movement details are present and accurate in the generated report.
data_to_capture: Specific transaction details from the report

acceptance_criteria: Cycle count schedules are generated accurately based on configured parameters.
Inventory movement reports are generated within 5 minutes and contain accurate transaction data for the specified period.
The system correctly identifies and highlights inventory discrepancies during cycle counting.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-008: Generate cycle count schedules using vendor's standard scheduling engine.
URS-INV-009: Create inventory movement reports using pre-built templates.
URS-INV-018: Generate inventory accuracy reports using standard reconciliation features.
data_integrity_requirements: Cycle count schedules must be comprehensive and accurate.
Inventory movement reports must accurately reflect all recorded transactions.
Discrepancies identified during cycle counts must be clearly reported.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Multi-Location Support and Reorder Alerts
test_cases.objective: To verify the system's capability to manage inventory across multiple storage locations and generate timely reorder alerts based on defined minimum stock levels.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
User has administrative privileges.
At least two distinct storage locations are defined in the system.
Several items are stocked in different locations with varying quantities.

test_steps.action: Navigate to the inventory management module and access the location management section.
test_steps.expected_result: The system displays a list of all configured storage locations.

test_steps.action: Verify that inventory items can be assigned to and tracked within specific storage locations.
test_steps.expected_result: Inventory quantities are accurately reflected for each item within its assigned location.
data_to_capture: Inventory quantities per item per location.

test_steps.action: For a selected item, reduce its stock level in a specific location to below its defined minimum stock level.
test_steps.expected_result: The system accurately updates the stock level for the item in the specified location.

test_steps.action: Trigger the reorder alert mechanism (e.g., by running a scheduled job or manually initiating the check).
test_steps.expected_result: A reorder alert is generated for the item whose stock level has fallen below the minimum threshold.
data_to_capture: Details of the reorder alert (item, location, quantity needed).

acceptance_criteria: The system successfully displays and allows management of multiple storage locations.
Inventory quantities are correctly associated with their respective storage locations.
A reorder alert is generated when an item's stock level drops below the predefined minimum.
The generated reorder alert contains accurate information about the item and the required action.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-010: Support multiple storage locations with standard location master setup.
URS-INV-011: Generate reorder alerts based on minimum stock levels using standard alerting.
data_integrity_requirements: Inventory quantities must be accurately maintained across all locations.
Reorder alerts must be generated based on correct stock levels and minimum thresholds.

test_cases.test_name: Verify ERP System Integration and Data Export to Excel
test_cases.objective: To verify the system's ability to interface with the existing ERP system and to export inventory data into an Excel format.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
User has appropriate access to the inventory management system and ERP system.
The ERP system is accessible and configured for integration.
Sample inventory data exists in the system.

test_steps.action: Initiate an inventory data synchronization process with the ERP system.
test_steps.expected_result: The system successfully communicates with the ERP system, and inventory data is exchanged as per the defined integration parameters.
data_to_capture: Any error logs or messages generated during synchronization.

test_steps.action: Verify that key inventory data (e.g., item codes, quantities, locations) in the inventory system accurately reflects the data in the ERP system after synchronization.
test_steps.expected_result: Inventory data is consistent between the inventory management system and the ERP system.
data_to_capture: Sample inventory data from both systems for comparison.

test_steps.action: Navigate to the reporting section and select an option to export inventory data to Excel.
test_steps.expected_result: The system presents an option to export data to Excel format.

test_steps.action: Execute the export function for a comprehensive inventory report.
test_steps.expected_result: An Excel file containing the selected inventory data is generated and downloaded.

test_steps.action: Open the downloaded Excel file and verify the accuracy and completeness of the exported data.
test_steps.expected_result: The Excel file contains all expected inventory data, formatted correctly, and matches the data within the system.
data_to_capture: Sample data from the Excel file for verification.

acceptance_criteria: The system successfully integrates with the ERP system, exchanging inventory data without errors.
Inventory data is consistent between the inventory management system and the ERP system post-synchronization.
The system allows for the export of inventory data to an Excel file.
The exported Excel file accurately and completely represents the inventory data from the system.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-020: Interface with existing ERP system using vendor's standard connectors.
URS-INV-021: Export inventory data to Excel format using built-in export functionality.
data_integrity_requirements: Data exchanged with the ERP system must be accurate and complete.
Exported data to Excel must be a true and accurate representation of the system's inventory data.

test_cases.test_name: Verify User Access Controls and Role-Based Security
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system enforces user access controls and role-based security as per URS-INV-017.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
User accounts with different roles (e.g., Administrator, Warehouse Operator, Viewer) are created.
Permissions for each role are defined in the system.

test_steps.action: Log in to the system using an Administrator account.
test_steps.expected_result: Administrator can access all system functionalities and settings.

test_steps.action: Log out and log in using a Warehouse Operator account.
test_steps.expected_result: Warehouse Operator can perform inventory management tasks (e.g., receiving, picking, moving) but cannot access administrative settings or user management.

test_steps.action: Log out and log in using a Viewer account.
test_steps.expected_result: Viewer can only view inventory data and reports, with no ability to modify or create records.

test_steps.action: Attempt to access functionalities restricted to other roles from each logged-in user session.
test_steps.expected_result: Access is denied for all unauthorized actions, with appropriate error messages displayed.

acceptance_criteria: Users can only access functionalities permitted by their assigned role.
Unauthorized access attempts are blocked and logged.
System correctly enforces role-based security.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-017: Support user access controls through vendor's role-based security.
data_integrity_requirements: User access logs are maintained.
Role definitions are accurate and consistently applied.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Inventory Audit Trail and Transaction History Archiving
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system maintains a comprehensive audit trail for all inventory transactions and that transaction history can be archived according to retention policies.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
Sufficient inventory transactions have been performed to populate the audit trail.
Vendor's data retention policies are understood and configured (if applicable).

test_steps.action: Perform a series of inventory transactions (e.g., receiving, issuing, adjusting quantity, changing location) for a specific item.
test_steps.expected_result: Each transaction is successfully recorded in the system.
data_to_capture: Details of each transaction (item, quantity, type, user, timestamp)

test_steps.action: Access the inventory audit trail report for the performed transactions.
test_steps.expected_result: The audit trail report accurately reflects all performed transactions, including user, date/time, transaction type, and any changes made.
data_to_capture: Comparison of report with performed transactions

test_steps.action: Verify that the audit trail includes details of user logins and logouts.
test_steps.expected_result: User login/logout events are present in the audit trail.

test_steps.action: Initiate the archiving process for historical transaction data based on vendor's retention policies (if manual archiving is supported or if a scheduled archive is to be verified).
test_steps.expected_result: Historical transaction data is successfully archived and no longer readily accessible in the active system, or the archive process completes as scheduled.
data_to_capture: Verification of data removal from active system (if applicable)

test_steps.action: Attempt to retrieve archived data (if applicable and supported by the system).
test_steps.expected_result: Archived data can be retrieved and is consistent with the original transaction records.
data_to_capture: Comparison of retrieved data with original records

acceptance_criteria: All inventory transactions are logged in the audit trail.
The audit trail provides sufficient detail to reconstruct transaction history.
Transaction history archiving is performed according to defined policies.
Archived data is retrievable and accurate.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-016: Maintain inventory audit trail using vendor's standard logging functionality.
URS-INV-019: Archive transaction history using vendor's data retention policies.
data_integrity_requirements: Audit trail is immutable and tamper-evident.
Archived data is stored securely and is accessible for the required retention period.
Data integrity is maintained throughout the archiving process.

test_cases.test_name: Verify System Performance Under Load and Concurrent User Access
test_cases.objective: To verify that the inventory management system can handle the specified number of SKUs and concurrent users without performance degradation.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured according to vendor specifications.
Test environment is set up with sufficient resources.
Test data representing 10,000 SKUs is loaded into the system.
User accounts for 25 concurrent users are created.

test_steps.action: Simulate 25 concurrent users performing typical inventory operations (e.g., receiving, picking, stock adjustments) for a sustained period.
test_steps.expected_result: Inventory updates are reflected within 30 seconds, and system response times remain within acceptable limits.
data_to_capture: System response times for various operations.
CPU and memory utilization of the system.

test_steps.action: Generate a complex inventory report (e.g., a full stock valuation report) while 25 users are actively using the system.
test_steps.expected_result: The inventory report generates within 5 minutes.
data_to_capture: Time taken to generate the report.

acceptance_criteria: Inventory updates are consistently reflected within 30 seconds.
System response times for all operations remain within acceptable thresholds.
Complex reports are generated within the specified 5-minute timeframe.
System resource utilization remains within acceptable levels during peak load.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-012
URS-INV-013
URS-INV-014
URS-INV-015
data_integrity_requirements: No data loss or corruption during high load.
Accurate reflection of inventory quantities.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Inventory Accuracy Reporting and Data Retention Policies
test_cases.objective: To verify the accuracy of inventory reports generated through reconciliation and ensure that transaction history is archived according to defined retention policies.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured.
Sufficient transaction history exists to test archiving.
Inventory data is available for reconciliation.

test_steps.action: Perform a cycle count and initiate a reconciliation process using the system's standard reconciliation features.
test_steps.expected_result: The system generates an inventory accuracy report highlighting discrepancies between physical counts and system records.

test_steps.action: Verify that the system correctly identifies and reports inventory discrepancies based on the reconciliation.
test_steps.expected_result: The accuracy report accurately reflects the identified discrepancies.
data_to_capture: Comparison of physical count data with report findings.

test_steps.action: Access and review archived transaction history that has exceeded the defined retention period.
test_steps.expected_result: Archived transaction history is accessible and remains intact as per the vendor's data retention policies.
data_to_capture: Verification of data integrity in archived records.

acceptance_criteria: Inventory accuracy reports accurately identify and quantify discrepancies.
Archived transaction history is retrievable and maintains data integrity.
The system adheres to the defined data retention policies for transaction history.
regulatory_basis: URS-INV-018
URS-INV-019
data_integrity_requirements: Accurate reporting of inventory discrepancies.
Preservation of historical transaction data.
Compliance with data retention policies.
